¿Cómo se hace un ANOVA de un factor?: How is a one-way ANOVA done?
Se compara la variabilidad entre grupos: The variability between groups is compared with that within: F = MSB/MSW, with MSB = SSB/(k − 1) and MSW = SSW/(N − k). With the groups 20 21 23 19 22, 24 26 25 27 23 and 29 28 31 27 30: means 21, 25 and 29, SSB = 160, SSW = 30, F = 80/2.5 = 32 with 2 and 12 d.f., which exceeds F₂,₁₂;0.95 = 3.885, so H₀ is rejected.
¿Qué hacer si el ANOVA sale significativ: What to do if the ANOVA is significant?
Solo dice que alguna media difiere. Para: It only says that some mean differs. To find out which, the pairs are compared with a t using MSW and the p-value is corrected for the number of comparisons (Bonferroni). The effect size is η² = SSB/SST, in the example above 160/190 ≈ 0.84.

Gráfica de los datos: puntos de cada gru: Graph of the data: points of each group with its mean, or lines of means for the interaction between the two factors
Se quiere saber si $k$ grupos tienen la: We want to know whether $k$ groups have the same mean. Instead of comparing groups two at a time, the variability between the group means is compared with the variability within each group: if the means are much farther apart than the noise within can explain, $H_0$ is rejected.
Supuestos y qué hacer si fallan: Assumptions and what to do if they fail
Observaciones independientes, residuos $: Independent observations, approximately normal residuals $x_{ij} − x̄_i$ (checked with Shapiro-Wilk) and similar variances (Levene, with the median, is robust; Bartlett is more powerful but is fooled if the data are not normal). With groups of equal size the test holds up quite well; if Levene rejects, use Welch's F, which weights each group by $n_i/s_i^2$ and adjusts the degrees of freedom, and compare the pairs with Games-Howell. If normality fails with little data, see Kruskal-Wallis in Non-parametric tests.
$η^2 = SC_E/SC_T$ es la proporción de la: $η^2 = SS_B/SS_T$ is the proportion of the total variability explained by the factor, but it tends to overestimate it with little data; $ω^2 = {SS_B − (k − 1) MS_W}/{SS_T + MS_W}$ corrects it. Cohen proposes $f = √{η^2/(1 − η^2)}$: 0.10 small, 0.25 medium, 0.40 large.
Si el ANOVA sale significativo no dice <: If the ANOVA is significant it does not say which means differ. Comparing all pairs with an ordinary t inflates the error: with 10 groups there are 45 pairs and, if all the means were equal, almost certainly one would come out “significant”. The methods control the error of the whole family:
<b>Tukey (HSD)</b> usa el rango studenti: Tukey (HSD) uses the studentized range $q = |x̄_i − x̄_j|/√(MS_W/2 · (1/n_i + 1/n_j))$; it is the usual choice for all pairs (Tukey-Kramer if the sizes differ).
<b>Bonferroni</b> multiplica cada p-valo: Bonferroni multiplies each p-value by the number of pairs; Holm does the same step by step and is always more powerful.
<b>Scheffé</b> es el más conservador, pe: Scheffé is the most conservative, but it works for any contrast, including those you think of after seeing the data.
<b>Games-Howell</b> no supone varianzas: Games-Howell does not assume equal variances: it uses that of each pair and its Welch degrees of freedom.
Si la pregunta se conoce antes de ver lo: If the question is known before seeing the data (for example, a control against the mean of the treatments) it is tested directly with $ψ = ∑ c_i x̄_i$, where $∑ c_i = 0$: $t = ψ/√(MS_W ∑ c_i^2/n_i)$ with $N − k$ degrees of freedom. For “A against the mean of B and C” the coefficients are 2, −1, −1.
Con dos factores A (de $a$ niveles) y B: With two factors A (with $a$ levels) and B (with $b$) and $n$ replicates in each cell, the variability is split into $SS_A$, $SS_B$, the interaction $SC_{AB}$ and the error $SS_E$; each effect is tested with $F = CM_{effect}/MS_E$. There is interaction when the effect of one factor depends on the level of the other (in the graph, non-parallel lines); if it is significant, interpret the main effects with care. The design must be balanced (all combinations, the same number of replicates); with a single data point per cell it is assumed there is no interaction and its variability is used as the error. The partial $η^2$ and $ω^2$ of each effect are given.
Las comparaciones por parejas (Tukey, Bo: Pairwise comparisons (Tukey, Bonferroni, Holm, Scheffé and Games-Howell) are chosen by hand: the tool does not decide for you which applies. With two factors there is no Games-Howell.
Supone que los grupos son independientes: It assumes the groups are independent, with approximately normal data and similar variances: the tool cannot check this for you with little data.
